assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a physical-chemistry achievement in lipid self-assembly: pH-dependent charge, bilayer and non-lamellar phase behaviour, and encapsulation of nucleic acids. They made siRNA and mRNA medicines practical, with enormous demonstrated societal impact including the COVID-19 vaccines. From a membrane and lipid colloid perspective the underlying chemistry is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) developed the early lipid-nanoparticle formulation, remote loading and ionizable-lipid concepts; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan made major later contributions on lipid design and delivery. Credit is crowded, so a three-person split is a judgement; Cullis, Hope and Madden best reflect the foundational lipid-assembly work as I understand it.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale over several years and independently reproduced; the 2023 Medicine prize recognised the mRNA modifications but not the delivery vehicle, so recognition of the carrier is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Anderson, Langer or MacLachlan should displace a Vancouver contributor is unresolved.
Patent disputes and the exact priority among ionizable-lipid designs are not settled in my knowledge.
Potential overlap with the already-recognised mRNA prize may lower committee appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as phase separation of proteins and nucleic acids. It is a physical-chemistry concept (thermodynamics of demixing, multivalency) with broad influence across cell biology and disease, and it connects directly to lipid and protein self-assembly.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's 2009 P-granule work is the usual origin, with Rosen's multivalent-protein phase separation work (2012) as the quantitative chemical foundation; Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-grammar theory and experiments. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen make a coherent trio, though the choice excludes strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Very rapid adoption, but debate persists on which in vivo assemblies are true liquid-liquid phase separation and on functional relevance, so interpretation is still settling.
uncertainties: Controversy over physiological relevance and the criteria for phase separation in cells.
Allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is contestable.
Possibly premature relative to rivals with settled interpretations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory give a statistical-mechanical solution to Levinthal's paradox and a unifying framework for protein folding, misfolding and aggregation, including amyloid assembly, which is close to my own field. It is conceptually deep, original and long-lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes introduced the funnel/spin-glass picture; Onuchic and Wolynes developed it extensively; Dill contributed lattice models and the hydrophobic-collapse view; Fersht supplied experimental phi-value mapping. I propose the theory core, Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill, though Fersht is a credible alternative for experimental grounding.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation by experiment and simulation; the framework is mature and now complemented by AI structure prediction, which was recognised in 2024, leaving the physical theory still without a prize.
uncertainties: Wolynes and Dill versus Fersht for a three-person configuration is unresolved.
Bryngelson's early role is hard to accommodate under the three-laureate limit.
Whether the committee views the contribution as theory-primarily physics-leaning.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure calculation and dynamics, enabling ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces, water and reactions. Its originality and lasting impact on chemistry and materials are very high, and it underpins much of modern condensed-phase simulation.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person attribution: the 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the decisive contribution, with little ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Nearly four decades of use and validation; recognition is arguably overdue, with the Chemistry 2013 prize covering multiscale methods rather than this approach.
uncertainties: Committee might fold this together with metadynamics or machine-learned potentials, changing credit for Parrinello.
Possible preference for experimental breakthroughs over methodology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase, giving stoichiometry, subunit architecture and, notably, intact membrane proteins with bound lipids. It is of direct interest from a lipid-protein interaction standpoint and has had deep impact in structural biology and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Robinson drove membrane-protein and lipid-binding applications and broad assembly analysis; Heck developed instrumentation and workflows for large complexes; Chait contributed early protein-complex methods; Loo and Gross have also contributed. The three-way split is a judgement among several pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted, though the 2002 prize already honoured electrospray ionization; the incremental step from soft ionization to native MS may be seen as less discrete.
uncertainties: Overlap with proteomics (Heck also appears there) and with the 2002 prize.
Fair credit among early pioneers is unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing of single nucleic-acid molecules turned a membrane channel into an analytical instrument, linking membrane biophysics, protein engineering and single-molecule chemistry, and leading to a commercial sequencing platform with real scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the 1996 principle; Bayley engineered alpha-hemolysin pores; Akeson showed enzyme-controlled translocation. Branton, Deamer and Bayley are plausible, but Akeson's practical step and Kasianowicz's first measurement complicate the split.
assessment.maturity: Technology is established and widely used, and independent platforms confirm the principle; the field is still maturing in protein sequencing.
uncertainties: Priority between Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer and the later engineering work is disputed.
Whether sequencing is chemistry rather than biology in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation using PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new modality in chemical biology and drug discovery that exploits induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases. It has produced clinical candidates and a conceptual shift in pharmacology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs; Ciulli provided structure-guided VHL ligands; the molecular-glue strand involves Handa, Ito and others (thalidomide mechanism), which would require a different split. A single prize may be hard to configure.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but no approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge, so the recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with PROTAC and glue branches needing different laureates.
Clinical outcomes are not yet confirmed.
Detailed credit for the earliest PROTAC concept is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a fast rise in solar-cell efficiency and opened a large field in materials and energy chemistry, with fascinating defect, ion-migration and phase-behaviour questions in soft crystalline solids.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells in 2009; Park and Snaith produced the key solid-state advances in 2012; Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also contributed. A trio of Miyasaka, Park and Snaith is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is confirmed independently, but long-term stability and commercialisation are unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Operational stability and toxicity concerns.
Disputed allocation among at least six credible contributors.
Premature versus other established candidates.
